facts.claim: Jain and Wallace (2019) found that attention weights often disagree with other measures of what mattered, and that very different attention patterns can give the same prediction.
nostalgebraist's logit lens (2020) reads a model's middle layers through its own final output step, and finds a fair guess often forms partway up and is refined after.
Meng and colleagues (2022) used causal tracing, copying activations between runs, and found GPT's factual recall runs through middle-layer MLPs as it reads the subject's tokens.
Turner and colleagues (2023) steer a model by taking the difference of its activations on two contrasting prompts and adding it during the forward pass, with no training.
Elhage and colleagues (2022) call it polysemanticity when one neuron responds to several unrelated things, and explain it with superposition: more features than neurons.
Anthropic (October 2023) split a 512-neuron layer of a small transformer into more than 4,000 features, each closer to one meaning than any neuron.
Anthropic (May 2024) extracted millions of features from the middle layer of Claude 3 Sonnet; turning up one for the Golden Gate Bridge made Claude say it was the bridge.
Anthropic's attribution graphs (March 2025) trace which features feed which on one prompt, through a replacement model whose MLPs are swapped for cross-layer transcoders.
Applied to Claude 3.5 Haiku (March 2025), the graphs showed it representing Texas on the way to answering Austin for the capital of the state containing Dallas.
Anthropic (March 2025): even on short, simple prompts, their method captures only a fraction of the computation Claude performs.
